lesson_title: The Desert the Jungle Built, and the Cake the Karoo Baked
hook_text: The Sahara exists BECAUSE it rains at the equator. Your Grade 11 exam runs on that one twist.
clip_script: Here is the twist that unlocks Grade 11 geography: the Sahara is the equator's fault. Hot equatorial air rises, rains itself empty over the jungle, drifts poleward, and comes back DOWN near 30 degrees — dry, heavy, cloud-crushing. Sinking air cannot rain, and 30 degrees is exactly where earth parks its great deserts. The jungle and the desert are two ends of one loop. Now slide that whole machine with the seasons: in summer the great rain seam dips south and soaks the Highveld with thunderstorms; in winter it retreats, the Kalahari High presses down like a lid, and the storm track finally reaches the Cape — which is why Cape Town gets soaked in July while Johannesburg gets frost. One machine, two opposite rain seasons. Then look down at what all that weather has been doing to the rock. The Karoo is a rained-on layer cake: hard dolerite icing over soft shale sponge, nibbled from the edges — wide table to small table to tall stump to bare cone. Plateau, mesa, butte, conical hill: the whole skyline is one dessert in four stages of being eaten. Tilt the layers and you get ridges with one lazy slope and one cliff face; skip the layers entirely and granite bakes as one loaf, peeling in curved crusts into the bald domes of Paarl. Weather upstairs, rock downstairs, one story — and the exam map is just its photograph.
visual_style: Animated globe with glowing circulation loops dropping deserts at 30 degrees; a sweeping rain band wiping across southern Africa with the seasons; a Karoo skyline morphing into a sliced layer cake and back; granite domes peeling in slow curved flakes.
mood: Revelatory and brisk, a chain of aha moments.
pacing: Cold-open twist, quick loop animation, seasonal slide beat, cake reveal played for delight, tight one-story close.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and own the machine upstairs and the rock downstairs before the paper.
